In the middle of the river on the Serbian and Romanian border, a broken-up hull was visible on a sandbank that is normally underwater. Other vessels were partly submerged, some still believed to be laden with weapons. View image in fullscreen The wreckage of a second world war German warship near Prahovo, Serbia on Tuesday. Volodymyr Zelenskyy said interceptor missile development must show ‘concrete results’ by the end of this year. Photograph: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: We will build missiles the way we built drones – Zelenskyy ‘Concrete results’ needed by end of the year in developing alternative to Patriot, says Ukrainian president. What we know on day 1,626 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Thu 6 Aug 2026 21.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymr Zelenskyy has said he wants “concrete results” by the end of this year on producing an anti-ballistic missile defence system for Ukraine. Photograph: Axel Schmidt/Reuters Germany Analysis The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor Initial evidence suggests aerial drone, found near Ukrainian cargo planes at German airport, came from Russia Wed 5 Aug 2026 13.32 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 14.53 EDT Share The armed drone found at Leipzig airport on Wednesday may not have exploded, but the fact that it got inside the perimeter, close to Ukrainian cargo planes , raises obvious concerns for the security of international aviation. Though the identity of the culprits is unknown, the initial evidence points firmly towards a Russian-orchestrated plot. It is the first time that a drone with explosives has been found in Europe far from the Ukrainian border. Photographs published by German newspapers show a quadcopter, a design familiar from the Ukraine war, with a package attached.
